gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the invalid interpolation estimate using the H1 seminorm instead of the full H1 norm, gives a nonzero constant counterexample, and supplies the corrected full-norm estimate. This directly captures why the estimate cannot be used for arbitrary errors without a zero-mean restriction.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries concern the same nonlinear interpolation step and its failure to control the L3 norm of an arbitrary error using only the H1 seminorm; constant components are uncontrolled, so the printed energy estimate is invalid.

component_coverage.gold_component: The interpolation estimate incorrectly uses the H1 seminorm for an arbitrary error, although the stability setting supplies no zero-mean condition and constant errors invalidate the bound.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly contrasts the full H1 norm with the seminorm, demonstrates failure on nonzero constants, and repairs the estimate with the full norm and the resulting additional L2 contribution.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns point-sampling an L2 equivalence class and the resulting ill-defined FV-FE initialization. ISSUE-001 instead concerns an interpolation inequality for an error function; it contains no diagnosis of representative dependence or point-evaluation well-definedness.

The gold issue is the underdetermined vector elliptic problem used to certify the gradient maximum norm, including missing tangential or natural boundary conditions. ISSUE-003 diagnoses a sign error and unbound time indices in an initial residual estimate, not the boundary-value problem or gradient certification.

The gold issue is an unsupported extension of existence results from smooth-boundary domains to bounded polygonal or mixed-boundary domains. ISSUE-001 concerns the validity and repair of a nonlinear energy estimate; its downstream mention of existence results does not recognize the missing domain-regularity theorem or hypothesis transfer.

The gold issue concerns circular use of a weak solution on [0,T] to prove that the solution exists through T, requiring localization below the maximal existence time. ISSUE-003 concerns the algebraic validity of an initial residual bound and does not identify the circular existence argument or its time-interval quantifier failure.
